A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TVM research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, figures and tables, are readable and support reliable comparison across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original GSM8K and MATH experiments, beam-size analyses, runtime measurements and additional Llama2 comparisons.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments, including REBASE evaluations, verifier-error analyses, compute measurements and appendix studies.

M1.justification: TVM retains the same prefix-based probability labels, empirical estimation algorithm, scalar-head architecture and verification plus language-modeling objectives. Algorithm 1 matches between v1 Appendix C and v2 Appendix B. REBASE is introduced as another experimental search strategy without modifying TVM.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K and MATH, with the same coverage involving MetaMath-fine-tuned models. The new diagnostics and search experiments introduce no additional dataset, domain or task coverage. Removing the Llama2 experiment changes model coverage rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: After matching Math-Shepherd with PRM and beam-search OVM with ORM, substantive changes remain: v2 adds PRM to the main beam-search comparisons and evaluates REBASE alongside the existing search strategies. It removes v1 Appendix B's comparison with Feng et al.'s sentence-level value model.

E3.justification: v2 introduces REBASE with K=40, token-value RMSE against empirical targets from 256 sampled paths, and precision-recall evaluation over 337664 GSM8K solutions with varying thresholds. It adds the beam setting (20,5) and removes the Llama2 K=10 experiment. The retained Best-of-N budget and 500-problem MATH evaluation split remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds aggregate value-estimation and PRM error analyses in Table 1 and Figure 3, prefix-overlap cases in Appendix D, and training-data generation cost measurements. It extends the existing beam-size and inference-runtime analyses with smaller beams and FLOPs, while replacing v1's illustrative failure cases.

E5.justification: v1 already reports three-trial means and standard deviations in Tables 3–4. v2 extends this reporting to existing Llama3/GSM8K and MATH TVM beam-search results previously presented as single values. The Mistral/GSM8K beam statistics are retained from v1 Table 3; no increase beyond three trials or new significance testing is stated.

E6.justification: At the retained Best-of-N N=256 setting, GSM8K/Mistral-7B-MetaMath TVM accuracy changes from 88.86 to 89.01. For MATH/Llama3-8B-MetaMath, Math-Shepherd/PRM changes from 43.40 to 44.40 while TVM remains 43.40, replacing their tie with a PRM lead. v2 also adds REBASE, verifier-diagnostic and compute results, and removes the Llama2 results.

T1.justification: Proposition 3.1 becomes Proposition 4.1 with equivalent assumptions and the same Appendix A proof. v2 Section 4.1 adds a token-generation complexity derivation contrasting quadratic per-token rollout costs with linear sampling costs for the retained prefix-sharing estimator.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes token-grained verification and general mathematical-reasoning improvements. v2 makes PRM false negatives and premature pruning central contributions, claims their first identification, and specifically argues that TVM improves tree search by reducing false negatives while maintaining comparable false-positive errors.

C2.justification: v2 develops a false-negative-based explanation of PRM failures and adds the qualification that insufficient prefix overlap makes later TVM labels collapse to binary outcome labels. It reinterprets the beam-size evidence as a compute tradeoff favoring (40,10), whereas v1 emphasized saturation at (100,25). The earlier resource-constraint and broader-application limitations paragraph is removed.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents training-data sampling costs and extends decoding-setting disclosures to REBASE. However, Appendix C omits the verifier-initialization rows provided in v1 Appendix E, and v1's explicit one-epoch verifier-training statements disappear. Most learning rates, batch sizes and sampling parameters are retained.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions the work around test-time compute, adding discussion and citations to Brown, Snell, Wu and newer automated process-supervision work. Much of v1's prompting and verifier-free planning context disappears, and the claimed identification of PRM false negatives becomes a new novelty argument.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Background and related-work material is reorganized into search-strategy and verifier-pitfall sections; the method explanation now introduces probability labeling before its value-model interpretation. Experimental details and analyses are substantially rearranged between the main text and appendices.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single-column ICLR layout. v2 redraws the supervision schematic, replaces case-study diagrams, adds precision-recall and histogram plots, and expands the result and compute tables. The prefix-label illustration is retained as Figure 4, and the beam-size table moves to Appendix E with additional content.

improvement.justification: The direct PRM beam-search comparisons and quantitative verifier diagnostics address an important gap in v1's tree-search argument, previously supported mainly by ORM comparisons and selected examples. REBASE evaluations and expanded compute analyses substantially strengthen the evidence. These gains outweigh the removed Llama2/Feng comparison and lost initialization and training-epoch disclosures, although those omissions weaken reproducibility.
